newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil posts $811 mln July trade gap - source.
newsitem.headline: Brazil posts $811 mln July trade gap - source.

text.p: Brazil posted a larger-than-expected trade deficit of $811 million in July, according to a government source who asked not to be identified.
A spokeswoman for the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said she could not confirm the figure.
According to the latest Reuters survey, analysts had expected a monthly trade gap of about $570 million.
Brazilian stocks tumbled on speculation about the deficit, with some estimates ranging as high as $814 million.
"That's wrong. It's $811 million," the source said.
National Globo television economics commmentator Miriam Leitao said during the lunchtime news that the trade deficit was $810 million last month.
She said it was caused by heavy oil imports by state-run Petrobras of some $133 million on July 31, coupled with zero soybean exports on the last day of the month.
The source said the July trade figures appeared to have leaked to the market Friday.
The leaked figures showed a trade deficit of $125 million on July 30 with exports of $191 million and imports of $316 million.
On July 31, the trade deficit was $203 million on exports of $209 million and imports of $412 million.
None of the figures could be officially confirmed.
